Flour + Water (SF). Other menus are partly visible at the left and right edges (a wine list and a beverage page with BEER); only the main white menu counts. Names are printed in capitals.
SF Restaurant Week set menu (Flour + Water). Fixed price 90 per person, 45 optional wine pairing; dishes have no individual prices. Wine pairings are printed in italics under each course.
Ren's Kitchen, Worthing. Four-column printed menu. Names printed in capitals. Prices in GBP without symbol.
Pizzaface, Worthing. Two-page spread. Names printed in capitals; V = vegetarian, vgn = vegan, (N) = contains nuts. Prices in GBP.
Cafe Rust, Brighton: drinks menu only, no food. Laminated brown card, prices without currency symbol.
The Greyhound, Kew. Printed pub menu; names in capitals with price and diet tags (V, VG, GF) on the same line. Prices in GBP.
The Shed: breakfast menu, 9AM - 11:30AM. Prices in GBP without symbol.

Alex's Kitchen (Indo-Chinese). Dense printed board; prices printed like 105-00 (INR). A further column is cut off at the LEFT edge of the photo (only its prices are visible) and must not be guessed. Glare hides the last five FISH prices.
Mothers Tacos (US). Laminated printed sheet, dense; mild glare on lamination. Prices in dollars with no $ sign.
Dyke Road Cafe (UK) lunch menu. Laminated printed sheet with a hard diagonal shadow across it. Prices in pounds, no symbol. Dietary tags (GF, VE) printed in italics after names.

photo_notes: Cafe Mondegar (Mumbai) table-top menu, HARD: two salt/pepper shakers block the centre, most of the sheet is out of focus, the CONTINENTAL MENU column is printed sideways (rotated 90 degrees), and the right edge is cut off so Lite Bites / Tandoor prices are missing. Only the rows below are legible; the yellow wine list at top is blurred and should NOT be required. A good model should say the photo is partly obstructed. NINE lines whose text is cut off mid-word at the right or bottom edge (Pollo Alla Pepe, Achari Gobi Tikka, Paneer Tikka, Chicken Tikka, Chicken Sheek, Fish Tikka, King Prawns Tikka, two naan lines) are LEFT OUT of the key: do not count them as found or as invented.

Gaggan (Bangkok) tasting menu "Best of Gaggan". Small, dim, low-resolution photo (1248x1856) with a faint watermark image behind the text. One fixed price for the whole menu; courses have no individual prices.

The Peg House Grill (US). Handwritten chalk/marker board behind glass, HARD: strong glare and reflections (the photographer is reflected in the lower half), several descriptions under the glare are only partly legible. Prices handwritten with $ and superscript cents; written here as plain numbers.

All entrees "served with beans and rice". Prices printed as "/ 19". TWO entree lines at the left edge (Chile Colorado, Arroz con Pollo) have their first letters cut off and are LEFT OUT of the key: do not count them as found or as invented.

photo_notes: Duck House Chinese Restaurant (US) takeout menu, two printed sheets taped to a wall, VERY dense (about 230 items), bilingual Chinese/English, chili icons and GF marks. Photo cuts the RIGHT edge of the top sheet (Pork prices) and the LEFT edge of the bottom sheet (first letters of Tofu & Vegetable names). Right-hand info panel (hours, phone, address) is cut off and not required. Chinese names are not transcribed. SEVEN Tofu & Vegetable lines at the left edge of the bottom sheet (broccoli, cauliflower, shredded potato, two A Choy lines, two pea lines) have their first letters cut off and are LEFT OUT of the key: do not count them as found or as invented.

Little Saint (Healdsburg, US) Summer 2022 printed menu on a wooden stand, indoor light, slight angle. Plant-based menu. Prices printed after a bullet; salads share one "7/13" price (two sizes) printed at the section header.

The Dwarf Grill (Hapeville, GA) 1940s reproduction menu card set into a table top, photographed at a steep angle; small print but sharp. Prices in cents ("20c"). Left panel is restaurant info only (name, address, motto, owners) and is not required.

Little Lou's (Sonoma County, US). Handwritten marker on kraft paper taped to a shop window; reflections and a Cheetos bag behind the glass. Short menu. "Coming soon... milkshakes" and "Hours" notes are not items.

The Block (US) "Happy Hour Specials" handwritten whiteboard; a different printed menu is partly visible at the LEFT edge (prices $24, $14, $3.50 and a gyro photo) and a mirror image of the board shows at the right - neither should be transcribed. "Riblets" has a taped-over correction.

Woodford General Store (US). Chalk A-frame board listing categories only - NO prices and no individual dishes. One bullet is empty (erased item). A good model should return these 7 items with empty prices and not invent any.

Boardwalk Bistro (Australia) specials chalkboard, handwritten capitals, some glare. "Taste of the Sea" is one shared plate made of four parts; only the Fish of the Day items have prices. The watermelon salad is written without a heading.

Mr. B's (US) letter-board menu behind glass, HARD/PARTIAL: close-up of one section only ("HOT SANDWICHES" header half cut at the top), the RIGHT edge is cut so prices lose their last digit on two rows and a second size column (after "REG") is missing entirely; strong reflections. Prices are letter-board digits without a decimal point (6 74 = 6.74). A good model should flag the photo as partial.

Hot Doug's (Chicago) "Today's Specials" printed cards on a wall board, clean and well lit. Ten sausages in two columns; small "$9.00"-style prices under each card. Read left column top to bottom, then right column.
